title: General & Fit
description: The motivation, fit, and practical questions most interviews open or close with, for any role.

questions.title: Tell Me About Yourself
questions.prompt: Tell me about yourself and what brings you to this role.
follow_ups: Which part of your background is most relevant to this job?
What is not on your resume that I should know?
questions.carl_focus: Keep it to about ninety seconds: where you are now, the two or three experiences that led here, and why this role is the next step.

questions.title: Walking Through Your Resume
questions.prompt: Walk me through your resume, including any changes of direction or gaps.
follow_ups: Which move taught you the most?
Is there a decision in there you would make differently now?
questions.carl_focus: Give each move a reason rather than a list of duties, and address a gap or a change of direction plainly in one sentence.

questions.title: Why This Company
questions.prompt: Why do you want to work here?
follow_ups: What do you know about what we do that most candidates would not?
What would make you turn this offer down?
questions.carl_focus: Name something specific about the company, connect it to work you have actually done, and say what you want to contribute.

questions.title: Why This Role
questions.prompt: What interests you about this role in particular?
follow_ups: Which part of the job do you expect to be hardest for you?
How is this different from what you do now?
questions.carl_focus: Point to two or three parts of the job itself, show you have done similar work, and be honest about what would be new.

questions.title: Why You're Moving On
questions.prompt: Why are you looking for a new position right now?
follow_ups: What would have had to change for you to stay where you are?
What have you learned about what you need from a job?
questions.carl_focus: Stay honest and forward-looking: say what you are moving toward, and avoid criticizing people at your current or last job.

questions.title: Why We Should Hire You
questions.prompt: Why should we hire you for this role?
follow_ups: What would you want to accomplish in your first ninety days?
What is the biggest gap between your background and this job?
questions.carl_focus: Match your two strongest qualifications to what the role needs most, with one piece of evidence for each.

questions.title: Where You See Yourself in Five Years
questions.prompt: Where do you see yourself in five years?
follow_ups: What skills do you need to build to get there?
How does this role move you toward that?
questions.carl_focus: Describe a direction rather than a job title, and tie it to how you would grow in this role.

questions.title: The Work You're Proudest Of
questions.prompt: What professional accomplishment are you most proud of, and why?
follow_ups: What part of that was hardest for you personally?
What would you do differently if you did it again?
questions.carl_focus: Choose one accomplishment, make your own part in it clear, and say what the result was and why it matters to you.

questions.title: Your Greatest Strength
questions.prompt: What would you say is your greatest strength?
follow_ups: Can you give me a recent example of it in action?
When has that strength worked against you?
questions.carl_focus: Pick one strength that matters for this job and back it with a short, specific example and its outcome.

questions.title: A Weakness You're Working On
questions.prompt: What is a weakness you are working on?
follow_ups: What have you done about it in the last six months?
How would a colleague know it has improved?
questions.carl_focus: Choose a real weakness, not a strength in disguise, then spend most of the answer on what you are doing about it and the evidence it is working.

questions.title: How You Work Best
questions.prompt: What kind of work environment and management style bring out your best work?
follow_ups: Tell me about a manager you worked well with. What did they do?
What do you do when the environment is not ideal?
questions.carl_focus: Be specific about what helps you do good work, give an example, and show you can adapt when you do not get it.

questions.title: Handling Pressure and Competing Deadlines
questions.prompt: How do you handle pressure when several deadlines land at once?
follow_ups: Tell me about the last time that happened.
How do you decide what not to do?
questions.carl_focus: Describe how you actually decide what comes first, with a recent example and how it turned out.

questions.title: Salary Expectations
questions.prompt: What are your salary expectations for this role?
follow_ups: How did you arrive at that range?
Other than pay, what matters most to you in an offer?
questions.carl_focus: Give a researched range rather than a single number, tie it to the role and location, and stay open about the full package.

questions.title: Your Questions for the Interviewer
questions.prompt: What questions do you have for me about the role, the team, or the company?
follow_ups: What would you most want to know before accepting an offer?
What would you ask the person who would be your manager?
questions.carl_focus: Ask two or three questions that show you have thought about doing the job, such as how success is measured or what the team finds hard right now.
